title: Safiyyah and Maymunah
hookLine: Safiyyah, taunted for her Jewish family, is defended by the Prophet ﷺ, and Maymunah's house becomes a place where a boy learns the night prayer

cards: A woman is crying, and the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, walks in and asks why. Safiyyah tells him what she heard. Someone in the household, Hafsah, had called her the daughter of a Jew.

It was meant to sting, and it did. Safiyyah came from a noble family of a Jewish tribe of Arabia, and that remark turned her family into an insult. What he says next is preserved in Tirmidhi's collection.

teach.b: He doesn't tell Safiyyah to forget her family, or to be ashamed of it. He turns the taunt inside out. You are the daughter of a prophet, he tells her, meaning Aaron.
Your uncle is a prophet, meaning Moses. And you are married to a prophet. So what is there for her to boast over you?
Then he says: Hafsah, be mindful of Allah. Look at what he did. The very thing used against Safiyyah, her descent, became the thing he honored.

The Qur'an names Aaron and Moses among the prophets, and Muslims honor them as such. He pointed her to that line and said: this is yours. A taunt about where she came from was answered by honoring where she came from.
Now Maymunah, the other name in today's title. Tradition remembers her as the last woman he married. One scene with her in it is gentle and ordinary.
Her nephew, Abdullah ibn Abbas, still a boy, slept over at her house one night, and he tells us in Bukhari what he saw: the Prophet rising in the night, making his ablution, and standing to pray.
The boy got up and stood beside him to join in, and the Prophet took hold of him and moved him around to his right side, where he should stand.

teach.h: A BOY LEARNS IN MAYMUNAH'S HOUSE.
teach.b: Ibn Abbas grew up to be a teacher himself, and this lesson he learned in Maymunah's house.
One wife, defended against a taunt. One wife whose home was open for a boy to learn.

how: Muslims honor Safiyyah bint Huyayy and Maymunah bint al-Harith among the mothers of the believers; the Prophet's answer to the taunt is retold from Jami' al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Abbas's night in Maymunah's house from Sahih al-Bukhari.

o: the Prophet's aunt, who taught the young Ibn Abbas
a wife from a desert tribe, known for her poetry
a wife from a Jewish family, honored for her descent

games.q: Safiyyah and Maymunah — tap the pairs.
p: called the daughter of a Jew
moved to the Prophet's right side

s: the Prophet told Safiyyah to forget her family
he told her she was the daughter of a prophet, with a prophet for an uncle.
he told Hafsah to be mindful of Allah
Tirmidhi reports it after he answered the taunt.
Ibn Abbas learned the night prayer by watching in Maymunah's house
Bukhari has him sleep over, rise to pray beside the Prophet, and be moved to his right.

games.q: you find your wife in tears; someone called her the daughter of a Jew. what do you say?
o: tell her she is the daughter of a prophet, her uncle a prophet, and married to a prophet.
tell her to answer back with an insult.
games.why: in Tirmidhi he honors her descent from Aaron and Moses, and tells Hafsah to be mindful of Allah.

practice: Bring to mind a remark you've heard aimed at someone's family, their background, their accent, their faith, maybe in a group chat, maybe at work.
Find what the Prophet found: something true and good in the very thing they were mocked for, and hold that sentence until it's ready. If you pray, ask for the courage to say it.

wordCard.voice: Safiyyah, taunted as the daughter of a Jew, and told by the Prophet that she was the daughter, niece, and wife of prophets. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the two names of today's mothers of the believers.

carryVoice: Your line: he defended her. Where she came from became her honor. Day eight hundred sixteen, done.
